michael: ran a focused benchmark on the mmap ringbuffer tokenizer today. quick summary: p50 dropped from ~8.2ms to 5.6ms when we batch frame reads, but p95 actually increased for small single-chunk requests. leaving raw traces below. :thinking:

sara: can you share the exact invocation and flags? :eyes:

michael: `./tools/bench_tokenizer --mmap-ring --concurrency=16 --duration=30s --payload=zipf-small`

raj: did you keep per-request proto parsing on? that used to dominate on small payloads

michael: yeah proto parsing was enabled (we wanted to measure end-to-end). flame excerpt: 
```
ingress.parse_total: 12.3ms
  mmap_read: 1.1ms
  frame_coalesce: 0.6ms
  tokenize: 3.2ms
  kvcache_lookup: 0.9ms
  proto_unmarshal: 4.5ms
  writev_flush: 1.0ms
```

emily: proto_unmarshal 4.5ms is surprising. are we allocating a new buffer per request then copying into it?

michael: looks like we do a small copy when converting iovec->bytebuf for the proto lib. also we do a per-request span allocation in tokenizer which shows up in alloc traces.

raj: two quick angles: try zero-copy proto views (if protobuf-lite) and reuse a per-thread span pool for tokenization buffers. also check grpc framing: fragmented messages can force extra copies when assembling.

michael: ran a micro where I enabled span-reuse and switched proto to view mode: p95 improved ~18% for small requests, p50 unaffected. micro command: `RING_POOL=1 PROTO_ZERO_COPY=1 ./tools/bench_tokenizer ...`

michael: also instrumented writev: we were flushing after every framed chunk instead of aggregating. change to aggregate up to 64KB before flush -> reduced syscall count by ~60% in traces.

emily: nice. did you see any memory pressure from the ring pool?

michael: negligible at our bench concurrency. but when we simulate high QPS with long sequences, the ring holds more spans — needs guard to avoid starving host RAM. added a simple LRU eviction on idle spans in test.

raj: another cost is grpc decompress path. if clients use gzip, server does an extra copy. consider negotiating no-compress for internal infra calls or offload to kernel splice where possible.

perf-bot: perf alert: post-deploy (deploy/2026-03-10) host-tokenize p95 +22% compared to baseline. Investigating related change: grpc chunking config rollback.

sara: action items: 
- michael: open PR with span-pool + writev aggregation + config flag for proto zero-copy (small, targeted). include perf numbers.
- raj: spike on grpc chunking defaults and decompress copy path (kernel splice viability).
- emily: add a regression test in perf harness: payload-dist zipf-small with concurrency 32 and assert p95 <= baseline*1.15.

michael: will draft PR today. attaching short perf snippet to the thread for visibility: 
```
before: p50 8.2ms p95 35.6ms syscalls/sec 420
after (span-pool+agg): p50 5.6ms p95 29.3ms syscalls/sec 165
note: enabling proto-zero-copy further reduced p95 to 24.0ms but requires proto lib change
```

emily: looks reasonable. please include a canary with traffic shaping to catch any tail regressions.

raj: also log the number of writev entries per request in prod for a week. we should watch for writev growth when batching overlaps with large payloads.

michael: agree. I'll add telemetry events: writev_count, mmap_reads, span_allocs. thanks all :thumbsup:
